chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Hashim ibn Khalid, from Nuaym al-Basri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The habitual drinker of the intoxicant is the one who, whenever he finds it, drinks it.

key_terms.مُدْمِنُ: The habitual drinker / one addicted to

ai.seo_question: What defines a habitual drinker of wine in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this definition by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that 'habitual consumption' (istihlak) is determined by the immediate urge and action upon availability, rather than just frequency. This criterion is pivotal in distinguishing between occasional indulgence and the state of being a 'mudmin,' which carries specific legal implications for prayer validity and testimony. It underscores the psychological and behavioral dimension of addiction in Islamic law.
